notes: The (b+1)/(B+1) figure (9.90e-07) assumes exchangeability; MCMC samples are autocorrelated, so the scan carries only n_eff = 4,372 effective samples (see joint_d2_ess). Zero exceedances supports an empirical bound of about 3/n_eff = 6.86e-04 (rule of three), not 9.90e-07. The sub-1e-06 headline rests on the parametric chi-squared(4) model (8.84e-07), stated as such.

What the scan shows without assuming Gaussianity: (a) 0 sampled plans reach the minority's D2; (b) at the two other maps' D2 the parametric model and the empirical tail are close (majority 0.1017 parametric vs 0.1011 empirical; enacted 0.0105 vs 0.0122). Two points do not validate the model at the minority's D2: between D2 16 and 24 the sample holds 1.6 to 3.0 times as many plans as the model predicts (findings/audit_2026-11-10/joint_sensitivity.json).
R-hat here is on the full 1,010,000-plan run; the s58a6-B table (2026-05-10) was computed at the run's 250,000-plan state.
